Terns mass trends over time

By age class and breeding status - issue #5 task 3

2026-09-08

1 Background

Issue #5 task 3 asks whether there’s a temporal trend in body condition (mass vs. year), per species. Extended per Inbal’s request to compare that trend across three groups, per species:

  1. Juveniles - this-year fledglings (EURING age 3), representing post-fledging condition.
  2. Adult breeders - spring-caught adults confirmed to have stayed to breed (the task 2c / any-year site-fidelity definition from 02_mass_analysis.Rmd).
  3. Adult non-breeders - spring-caught adults with no summer sighting in any year (presumed passage migrants, not confirmed as Atlit breeders).

This checks whether a mass trend (if any) is driven by a specific age/breeding-status class, rather than the population as a whole.

2 Data loading

raw_dir <- "../data_raw"
if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) raw_dir <- "data_raw"
stopifnot(dir.exists(raw_dir))

proc_dir <- "../data_processed"
if (!dir.exists(proc_dir)) proc_dir <- "data_processed"

out_dir <- "../output"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) out_dir <- "output"

ringing_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "ringing_data_raw.xlsx")
stopifnot(file.exists(ringing_path))

col_names_47 <- c(
  "CR1","RingReplace","Rec","RingPrefix","RingNum","Species","Sex","Age","Wing","Weight",
  "Date","Time","Place","Lat","Lon","Ringer","Country","Remarks","Net","CR2","Subsp","Tail","Head",
  "Breeding","CP1","CP2","CP3","CP4","Colour","D","M","OrigDate","OrigCountry","OrigLat","OrigLon","OrigAge",
  "OldCR1","OldCR2","OldCR3","OldMetal1","OldMetal2","OilHead","OilWings","OilUpperP","OilUnderP","OilLegs","OilSum"
)
raw <- read_excel(ringing_path, sheet = "Data", skip = 2, col_names = col_names_47)

terns <- raw %>%
  filter(Species %in% c("STEALB", "STEHIR")) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(Date),
    month = month(Date),
    ring_id = paste0(trimws(RingPrefix), RingNum),
    is_new = is.na(Rec) | trimws(Rec) == "",
    species_label = ifelse(Species == "STEHIR", "Common Tern", "Little Tern")
  )

3 Building the three comparison groups

3.1 Juveniles (age 3, Jun-Aug)

Unlike the adult analyses (spring, Mar-May), juveniles can only be measured once they’re in the nest/newly fledged, i.e. during the breeding season. Window is Jun-Aug here (wider than the Jun-Jul used for adult breeding-season mass in task 2) because juvenile catches remain substantial into August (e.g. Common Tern age-3 catches: Jun=106, Jul=1442, Aug=1049 - dropping the August tail would discard a large, non-trivial share of the juvenile data for no analogous reason to why adults were restricted to Jun-Jul).

juvenile_records <- terns %>%
  filter(is_new, Age == 3, !is.na(Weight), month %in% 6:8)

juvenile_mass <- juvenile_records %>%
  group_by(year, Species, species_label) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(Weight), sd_weight = sd(Weight), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(group = "Juvenile")

3.2 Adult breeders vs. non-breeders (spring weight, any-year confirmed)

Same construction as task 2c in 02_mass_analysis.Rmd: any adult (new ringing or recapture) weighed in spring (Mar-May), flagged as a confirmed breeder if that ring was also recorded (recapture or resighting) in June/July of any year.

juvenile_ages <- c(1, 3)

summer_ring_ids_anyyear <- terns %>%
  filter(month %in% 6:7) %>%
  distinct(ring_id) %>%
  pull(ring_id)

spring_adults_anyyear <- terns %>%
  filter(!(Age %in% juvenile_ages), !is.na(Weight), month %in% 3:5) %>%
  mutate(confirmed_breeder_anyyear = ring_id %in% summer_ring_ids_anyyear)

adult_mass_by_year <- spring_adults_anyyear %>%
  group_by(year, Species, species_label, confirmed_breeder_anyyear) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(Weight), sd_weight = sd(Weight), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(confirmed_breeder_anyyear, "Adult breeder", "Adult non-breeder")) %>%
  select(-confirmed_breeder_anyyear)

3.3 Combined

combined_by_year <- bind_rows(
  juvenile_mass,
  adult_mass_by_year
) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Juvenile", "Adult non-breeder", "Adult breeder")))

# Individual-level records, for the regression/trend tests below
combined_records <- bind_rows(
  juvenile_records %>% mutate(group = "Juvenile"),
  spring_adults_anyyear %>% mutate(group = ifelse(confirmed_breeder_anyyear, "Adult breeder", "Adult non-breeder"))
) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Juvenile", "Adult non-breeder", "Adult breeder")))

4 Visual comparison

ggplot(combined_by_year, aes(year, mean_weight, color = group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~species_label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Mean mass by year, age class and breeding status",
       y = "Mean weight (g)", x = "Year", color = "Group") +
  theme_minimal()

5 Trend statistics

Individual-level linear regression of Weight ~ year, per species and group (not just correlating the per-year means, so each year is weighted by its actual sample size):

trend_stats <- combined_records %>%
  group_by(species_label, group) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%   # need at least 3 years' worth of individual points to fit a trend
  group_modify(~ {
    m <- lm(Weight ~ year, data = .x)
    s <- summary(m)
    tibble(
      n = nrow(.x),
      n_years = n_distinct(.x$year),
      slope_g_per_year = round(coef(m)["year"], 3),
      se = round(s$coefficients["year", "Std. Error"], 3),
      p_value = signif(s$coefficients["year", "Pr(>|t|)"], 3),
      r_squared = round(s$r.squared, 3)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(trend_stats, caption = "Weight ~ year regression, by species and group")

Common Tern Adult breeder 490 16 -0.554 0.114 1.60e-06 0.046

6 Does the trend differ between groups?

Interaction test (Weight ~ year * group) per species - tests whether the year-slope itself differs significantly across juveniles / non-breeders / breeders, rather than just looking at each group’s trend in isolation:

for (sp in c("Common Tern", "Little Tern")) {
  d <- combined_records %>% filter(species_label == sp)
  m <- lm(Weight ~ year * group, data = d)
  a <- anova(m)
  p_interaction <- signif(a["year:group", "Pr(>F)"], 3)
  cat("**", sp, "**: year x group interaction p =", p_interaction, "\n\n", sep = "")
}

Common Tern: year x group interaction p =0.00648

Little Tern: year x group interaction p =0.0301

6.1 Interpretation

A significant interaction means the mass trend over time is not the same across groups (e.g. breeders declining while juveniles don’t, or vice versa) - that’s the more informative result for the paper than any single group’s trend alone. A non-significant interaction means whatever trend exists (if any) is roughly parallel across groups. Read this alongside the per-group trend_stats table above and the plot - small per-year-per-group sample sizes (see n columns) mean isolated significant/non-significant results for any one group should be treated cautiously.

7 Save outputs

write.csv(combined_by_year %>% select(-species_label), file.path(proc_dir, "mass_trends_by_group.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(trend_stats, file.path(proc_dir, "mass_trends_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("Wrote data_processed/mass_trends_by_group.csv and mass_trends_stats.csv\n")
